name: Brain Scan (VST3)
description: A free Windows VST3 synth that stores no waveforms. A specimen is a VOLUME - a scalar field filling a cube, exactly the kind of number a scanner records - and a scan line is a curve through it: one cycle of the sound is the field read along that curve. Bend the curve and the timbre changes because the curve is now somewhere else in the body; a closed loop has no edge and sounds soft, an open segment jumps once per cycle and sounds bright, a corner is a kink at a fixed phase, WARP reads the same shape unevenly. The filter's cutoff and the modulator are the same mechanism read slower - two more curves - and one SCAN control blends the GEOMETRY of two anchor lines before anything is read, so halfway between two sounds is tissue neither of them has visited. Nine specimens, seven of them fields built to give ordinary useful waveforms, plus a hollow shell and a simulated brain with skull, cortical folds, a fissure and ventricles. Lines are drawn on a tomography slice that you drive through the body, and watched in a ray-marched gantry where they glow inside the tissue until the density closes over them. The Brokild World FX rack and five macros. Every claim measured: two benches, 62 checks.
note: Windows VST3 · build 260904.1 · free download · 9 specimens · 9 factory patches · hints on every control · 17-page manual.
